It used to be 'superseded' at depth 1 and 'its_own_superseded' below, which is TWO NAMES FOR ONE RELATION and is exactly why the chain could only be pinned one depth at a time: a generic walk stops at the first name it does not recognise, and the coordinator's first attempt at this patch did precisely that, reading the chain as (104, 98) and stopping. Caught by running the test, not by reading it. tests/test_ci_gate.py now asserts the legacy key is absent, so the shape cannot come back.

superseded.why_it_was_wrong: Not wrong -- EXPIRED AS DECLARED. The 2026-08-19 entry named 'merge of P5.2' as its expiry. Observed delta +6. The coordinator's own predictions of that delta were wrong TWICE and are recorded because the pattern matters: '+1' on 2026-08-19 (read from a test file that then grew from 89 to 146 tests) and '>=4' on 2026-08-23 (counting skip SITES, which undercounts because one is parametrised). The protocol -- merge, read the observed number, commit it -- got it right both times without a prediction.

Not wrong -- EXPIRED EXACTLY AS PREDICTED. The 2026-08-17 entry declared 're_measure_required_at: merge of P5.1' and forecast 'roughly +25 skips ... this ceiling WILL breach on that merge, and it is meant to'. Observed delta: +26. The mechanism worked; the number was stale.

It came from a simulated runner on the dev machine, and the simulation was defeated by usrmerge: the harness removed `sumo` from a symlink copy of /usr/bin but left /bin on PATH, and /bin IS /usr/bin on this system, so shutil.which('sumo') kept finding it and 10 SUMO-gated tests ran that a runner skips. The error was invisible locally and was caught by the first real run -- which is the reason the ceiling was declared provisional and the branch was pushed.

ceiling_is_a_consequence_of: the workflow does NOT build the vendored CityFlow (coordinator ruling 2026-08-17: an unverified C++ build step is a new failure surface on the one task whose purpose is reliability). 32 of these 104 skips are cityflow-gated, so building it would move the ceiling from 104 to 72. CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this entry read '32 of these 72 ... from 72 to 40' and had survived TWO ceiling moves (72 -> 98 -> 104) unedited, because the only assertion over it was a substring grep, assert '40' in json.dumps(block), and that assertion EXPIRED rather than having always been empty. Measured 2026-08-24 on both eras: with the alternative deleted the expression is False on the 98-era file (4866d52) and True on this one, because the 104 measurement itself introduced the string '1240 passed' into measured.result. A substring assertion's discriminating power is a function of data it does not name, so it can stop discriminating with nobody editing it. The arithmetic is now pinned to ceiling_if_cityflow_were_built instead.

re_measure_required_at.event: merge of P5.3 (the no-RTG / context-length ablations), or any task adding corpus-gated tests
re_measure_required_at.reason: The ceiling is a COUNT of environment-gated skips, not a policy, so every task that adds a corpus-, CityFlow-, SUMO- or matplotlib-gated test moves it: it is stale by construction after any such merge, and a stale ceiling stops gating without saying so. RESTORED 2026-08-24 -- this field was dropped in 69680fa while ci_gate.py:39 still declares it part of the format and ci_gate.py:308 still reads it through a .get(..., '') default, so its absence printed an empty clause into every job summary instead of failing. tests/test_ci_gate.py:687 caught it; the gate could not.
re_measure_required_at.predicted_delta: NOT PREDICTED -- deliberately. Two coordinator predictions of this delta have been wrong; the protocol below does not need one.
re_measure_required_at.what_to_do: Merge, let this gate go red, download `ci-artifacts-<leg>` and classify junit.xml's <skipped> messages, then commit the observed value with its breakdown. Do NOT pre-bump and do NOT widen with slack: slack is what blinds the gate.
re_measure_required_at.mandated_by: coordinator ruling on BRIEF_23 Q1, 2026-08-17 -- 'a ceiling whose expiry lives only in a chat is a ceiling that silently breaches'.

pytest.how_to_update: Read the observed count from the failing job's summary, re-measure deliberately, and commit the new value together with the reason in the same commit. Never widen it with slack: slack is what blinds the gate.

english.pending_patch: 4 is the POST-APPLY total and requires docs/patches/check_english_mikolaj.patch, which adds 'Mikolaj' to ALLOWED_NAMES. Until a human applies it the tree measures 6 and THIS GATE REPORTS A MISMATCH ON PURPOSE, so the pending action cannot be forgotten. The regression that took it from the recorded 5 to 6 is docs/returns/P8.3.md:141, where the packet documents the allowlist gap BY WRITING THE NAME, making the sentence an instance of the defect it describes. Applying clears two hits (README.md:30 and that line), both carrying l-stroke and n-acute from 'Mikolaj Wolinski'.
english.by_file_note: by_file is the POST-APPLY enumeration and sums to total (4). README.md:30 was dropped on 2026-08-19: it carries l-stroke and n-acute from 'Mikolaj Wolinski' and clears when docs/patches/check_english_mikolaj.patch is applied, so leaving it listed would send the next auditor looking for a finding that is not there. docs/returns/P8.3.md:141 never enters this list for the same reason -- it clears with the same patch. WARNING FOR WHOEVER NEXT EDITS ci_gate.py: nothing mechanically asserts sum(by_file) == total. compare_to_baseline only visits observed paths and flags seen > known, so a file dropping to zero is silent and a by_file that disagrees with its own total passes the gate. That inconsistency was introduced in 96e12f8 by updating total and not its enumeration, and caught by a human reader. One assertion at load time would close it permanently.

frozen_guard.why: The guard derives everything from `git status --porcelain`, which is clean on a fresh checkout, so on a runner it always passes and proves nothing. It is invoked anyway because its absence would be worse, and the workflow says so at the call site rather than letting a green tick imply more than it proves. A PR-diff variant is a NEW enforcement mechanism and needs its own authorisation -- coordinator ruling 2026-08-17, parked as a DEFERRED row.
